questions.question: A driver should always:
questions.explanation: While driving, watch the road ahead for hazards. Know what you will do if a hazard becomes dangerous.

questions.question: If transporting explosives, you may leave your vehicle unattended:
questions.explanation: You may only leave a vehicle with explosives unattended in a safe haven. A safe haven is an approved location for parking vehicles loaded with explosives.

questions.question: If a tire fails, you should:

options.text: Loosen your grip on the steering wheel.
Check your tires after you stop completely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your tires after you stop completely.
questions.explanation: If a tire fails, grip the steering wheel firmly. Do not brake hard. Let the vehicle slow down on its own. Once it slows down, brake gently and pull off the road. Then check your tires.

questions.question: When an engine starts:

options.text: Warning lights should turn on, then turn off quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning lights should turn on, then turn off quickly.
questions.explanation: After the engine starts, warning lights and buzzers should turn off within a few seconds. If they stay on, something may be wrong with the vehicle.

questions.question: Proper coupling technique:

options.text: Is the same on all vehicles.
Is critical for safe vehicle operation.
Includes keeping the fifth wheel plate ungreased.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is critical for safe vehicle operation.
questions.explanation: Knowing how to couple and uncouple properly is essential for safe operation of combination vehicles. Wrong coupling can be very dangerous.

questions.question: If you feel tired before driving, you should:

options.text: Drive fast to reach your destination quickly.

questions.explanation: Caffeine will not help fatigue. It may keep you awake, but it will not make you more alert. When you feel tired, your body needs sleep. The only answer is to stop driving and rest.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver crashes on the road ahead of you, you should:

options.text: Block the driver in with your vehicle.
Stop at a safe distance and tell police about the driver's aggressive behavior.
Pull over and yell at the driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop at a safe distance and tell police about the driver's aggressive behavior.
questions.explanation: If you see a crash involving an aggressive driver, stop a safe distance away. Wait for police and tell them about the aggressive driving you saw.

questions.question: Driving at night is:

options.text: Safer than driving during the day.
Just as safe as driving during the day.
More dangerous than driving during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: More dangerous than driving during the day.
questions.explanation: Driving at night is more dangerous. You cannot see hazards as easily. Headlight glare affects vision. There are more tired and impaired drivers on the road.

questions.question: When checking a tank vehicle, the most important thing to verify is:

options.text: There is no frost on the windshield.

questions.explanation: Tank vehicles have many items to check during pre-trip inspection. Check your vehicle's manual for specific instructions. The most important check is to make sure there are no leaks.

questions.question: Engine belts should be:
questions.explanation: Check engine belts for tightness and wear. The right amount of slack varies by engine, so learn what is correct for your vehicle.

questions.question: When checking your vehicle's lights before driving, what should you do?

options.text: Keep the engine running and the vehicle in gear.
Check the lights from inside the vehicle.
Check the lights using a reflection from a shiny surface.

questions.explanation: To check your vehicle's lights, turn off the engine and remove the key. Set the parking brake. Turn on your low beam headlights and four-way flashers. Get out of the vehicle and make sure all lights are working.

questions.question: Which agency conducts the security check for a HazMat endorsement?
questions.explanation: To get a hazardous materials endorsement, you must pass a security check from the Transportation Security Administration (TSA).

questions.question: What do you need to know to choose the right hazardous materials placards?

options.text: The hazard classes of the materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: The hazard classes of the materials.
questions.explanation: To choose the right placards, you must know the hazard class of the materials, the amount being shipped, and the total weight of all hazardous materials in the vehicle.

questions.question: What helps other drivers see your vehicle?

options.text: Headlights turned off during the day.
Headlights used only in the rain.

questions.explanation: Keep your headlights clean. This helps them shine brightly so other drivers can see your vehicle.

questions.question: What do you test by pulling out the trailer air supply control?
questions.explanation: Test the trailer emergency brakes before driving. Pull out the trailer air supply control or place it in the "emergency" position. Pull forward slightly and make sure the trailer does not move.

questions.question: What letters appear on shipping papers and packages when a reportable quantity of a substance is being transported?
questions.explanation: When a substance is transported in a reportable quantity, the shipper must display the letters "RQ" on the shipping paper and package.

questions.question: How do you test the trailer service brakes?

options.text: Move forward slowly and apply the brakes with the brake pedal.
Reverse slowly and apply the brakes with the hand control.
Reverse slowly and apply the brakes with the brake pedal.
Move forward slowly and apply the brakes with the hand control.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move forward slowly and apply the brakes with the hand control.
questions.explanation: Make sure the braking system has normal air pressure. Release the parking brake. Move forward slowly and apply the brakes using the hand control. If the service brakes work properly, you will feel them activate.

questions.question: What should you do if the coolant temperature gauge rises above the highest safe level?

options.text: Pull over safely and check the problem.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over safely and check the problem.
questions.explanation: A high coolant temperature may mean the engine could fail or catch fire. Stop as soon as you safely can and find out what is wrong.

questions.question: Which type of cargo is hardest to transport because of shifting weight?
questions.explanation: Liquids in a partially-filled tank are difficult to transport. Liquids shift and surge when the vehicle moves, which causes the vehicle's weight to shift.

questions.question: What is the easiest way to tell if your trailer is skidding?

options.text: Use your mirrors to see if the trailer has left its lane.
Release the brake pedal and push it down again.
Watch for a jackknife warning light on the dashboard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your mirrors to see if the trailer has left its lane.
questions.explanation: Use your mirrors to spot a trailer skid. When you brake hard, check your mirrors to make sure your trailer is still in its proper lane.
